content:
As WhatsApp's official rollout of the username feature approaches, the messaging app now allows users to save a contact's username alongside their name and phone number. Details below.

The username field when adding new contacts has started rolling out to some WhatsApp users

Although usernames have long been a common feature on most messaging platforms, WhatsApp has only recently begun moving away from relying solely on phone numbers to identify users.

WhatsApp had earlier begun rolling out a username reservation mechanism, allowing users to claim their preferred handle before the feature officially launches, to prevent impersonation and scams.

A few weeks ago, WhatsApp began enabling the username feature for some iPhone users.

Now, according to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp has started supporting a username field when adding new contacts. The field is positioned between the last name/first name fields and the phone number field.

WABetaInfo reports:

WABetaInfo noted that whether on the beta or stable version of WhatsApp, this username field is being gradually pushed out to some users.

When the author tested with the latest stable version, the field does appear, but even entering an existing username shows the message "This username is not on WhatsApp".

That said, this is undoubtedly another step forward for WhatsApp to catch up with its competitors, plugging a basic feature that many have felt was long missing.
